Hello! My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm so glad you're here today, and I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you've undergone recently. Becoming a new mother can be a life-altering experience, and it's completely normal to have a wide range of emotions during this time.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS, a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and coping during the postpartum period. The purpose of this assessment is to identify any potential concerns or areas where you might need some extra support, so we can work together to ensure you have the best possible experience as a new mother.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm here to create a safe, supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. I want you to feel comfortable and at ease throughout our conversation.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your emotional well-being over the past week. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this process as comfortable and natural as possible.

So, let's get started. I'd like to begin by asking: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. (pausing, looking down) To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still find some things funny, like when my baby does something cute, but it's just not the same as before. I don't feel as carefree, I guess. (sighing) Most days, I just feel so tired and overwhelmed, it's hard to find the energy to laugh or enjoy things like I used to. Even when I do manage to laugh, it feels a little forced, you know? Like, I'm trying to be happy, but it's not really genuine. (looking up, with a hint of sadness) Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking my head) No, not really. Like I said, it's just not the same as before. I feel like I'm just going through the motions most of the time. I'll watch a funny video or see something that would normally make me laugh, but it just doesn't have the same effect on me now. (pausing, looking down) I don't know, maybe it's just the lack of sleep or the stress of taking care of a new baby, but everything just feels so much more serious and overwhelming now. (sighing) I miss feeling carefree and being able to laugh easily, but it's just not something that comes naturally to me right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head slightly) Not really. I mean, I used to love doing things like going out with friends, trying new restaurants, or just relaxing at home with a good book. But now, everything just feels like so much effort. (sighing) Even things that I used to enjoy, like taking a walk or watching a movie, just don't seem as appealing to me anymore. I feel like I'm just too tired or too worried about the baby to really enjoy anything. (pausing, looking down) And when I do try to do something I used to like, I just feel guilty for taking time away from my baby. It's like, I feel like I should be spending every waking moment with her, and that makes it hard for me to enjoy anything else. (looking up, with a hint of sadness) I just feel like I've lost myself a bit, you know.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Yeah... I do that a lot, actually. I feel like I'm not doing enough for my baby, or that I'm not doing things right. And when she cries or gets fussy, I immediately think it's because I'm not doing something correctly. (sighing) I'll be sitting there, trying to feed her or soothe her, and I'll just start thinking about all the things I could be doing better. Like, "If only I had done this" or "If only I had done that". (shaking my head) It's like, I know it's not rational, but I just can't help feeling like I'm somehow failing her. And it's not just with the baby, either. I'll be doing laundry or cleaning the house, and I'll think, "I should be doing this faster" or "I should be doing that better". (looking up, with a hint of guilt) It's just this constant feeling of not being good enough, I guess.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding, looking concerned) Oh, yeah... that's me, all the time. I worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is she sleeping too much? Is she too hot or too cold? (laughing nervously) I mean, it's like, I know these are normal things to worry about, but it feels like my mind is just constantly racing with worst-case scenarios. (biting my lip) And it's not just during the day, either. I'll be lying in bed at night, trying to sleep, and my mind will just start racing with all these what-ifs. What if the baby stops breathing? What if there's a fire in the house? What if... (trailing off, looking anxious) It's just this constant feeling of being on edge, like I'm waiting for something bad to happen. (sighing) And it's hard to calm myself down, you know? I'll try to tell myself that everything is okay, that the baby is safe and healthy, but my mind just won't listen. (looking up, with a hint of desperation) It's exhausting, to be honest.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath, looking nervous) Yeah... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. (shaking my head) It's hard to explain, but it's like my heart starts racing and my mind starts racing, and I just feel like I'm going to... I don't know, lose control or something. (looking down, fidgeting) It's like, I know it's not rational, but I just feel so overwhelmed and scared, like something bad is going to happen. (pausing, taking another deep breath) And it's not just when I'm alone with the baby, either. Sometimes it happens when my partner is home, or when we're out in public. (looking up, with a hint of fear) It's like, I'm just waiting for something to go wrong, and that feeling of panic is always lurking just beneath the surface. (swallowing hard) It's really scary, to be honest. I don't know how to make it stop. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling overwhelmed) Oh, yeah... that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the house, trying to be a good partner... it's all just so much. (sighing) And it's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too, like laundry and dishes and cooking meals. (laughing slightly) I mean, I used to be able to handle all that stuff without even thinking about it, but now it just feels like too much. (shaking my head) I feel like I'm drowning in responsibility, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) Some days, it feels like I'm just barely getting by, you know? Like, I'm just going through the motions, trying to survive until bedtime, and then I can just collapse. (looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) It's not how I thought motherhood would be, that's for sure. I thought I'd be happy and fulfilled, not feeling like I'm just trying to keep my head above water all the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yeah... that's been me, a lot. I mean, I'm already exhausted from taking care of the baby, but then I'll lie in bed at night and my mind will just start racing. (sighing) I'll think about all the things I need to do, or worry about the baby, or just feel overwhelmed by everything. (shaking my head) And it's hard to turn it off, you know? I'll try to relax, try to calm myself down, but my mind just won't quiet. (looking down) Some nights, I'll wake up in the middle of the night and just lie there, feeling anxious or sad, and I won't be able to go back to sleep. (pausing, feeling a lump form in my throat) It's like, I'm just so unhappy and overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop. (looking up, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) And then, of course, I'll feel guilty about being unhappy, because I have this beautiful baby and I should be grateful, right? (laughing slightly, feeling a sense of sadness) But it's hard to feel grateful when you're just feeling so lost and overwhelmed all the time.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a sense of sadness) Yeah... that's been me, a lot. I mean, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. (sighing) It's like, I'm supposed to be happy, I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my new baby, but instead I just feel empty and sad. (looking down, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes I'll be with my partner or friends, and they'll be trying to talk to me or make me laugh, and I'll just feel like I'm going through the motions. (shaking my head) I'll put on a smile, but inside, I'm just feeling so sad and lost. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's like, I'm grieving the person I used to be, I guess. I'm grieving the freedom and the independence I used to have. (looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) And I don't know how to get that back, or how to be happy again. (my voice cracking) Sometimes I just feel like I'm drowning in this sadness, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yeah... I've been crying a lot, actually. (pausing, looking down) It's like, the smallest things will just set me off, and I'll just start sobbing. (sighing) I'll be changing the baby's diaper, or feeding her, and suddenly I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and I'll start crying. (shaking my head) It's like, I'm trying to be strong, I'm trying to be a good mom, but it's just so hard. (looking up, feeling tears prick at the corners of my eyes) And it's not just when I'm alone, either. Sometimes I'll be with my partner, and I'll just start crying, and they'll be like, "What's wrong?" And I'll be like, "I don't know, I just feel so sad and overwhelmed." (laughing slightly, feeling a sense of embarrassment) It's like, I'm just a mess, emotionally. (pausing, taking a deep breath) But it's not just the big things, either. Sometimes it's just the little things, like the baby won't stop crying, or I'm just feeling so tired and exhausted. (looking down, feeling tears fall) And I'll just start crying, because I feel like I'm just not doing enough, or I'm not good enough. (my voice cracking) It's like, I'm just so unhappy, and I don't know how to make it stop.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down, and speaking in a barely audible whisper) Yeah... it has. (pausing again, taking a deep breath) I don't know, it's just... sometimes it feels like everything is too much, and I don't know how to make it stop. (looking up, with a hint of desperation) And I know it's not rational, I know it's not the answer, but... (trailing off, struggling to find the words) Sometimes it just feels like it would be easier if I wasn't here anymore. (quickly looking down, feeling a sense of shame and guilt) But I don't really mean that, I don't think. I mean, I love my baby, and I love my partner, and I don't want to hurt them. (pausing, taking another deep breath) It's just... I don't know, it's like this darkness inside of me, and it's telling me that I'm not good enough, that I'm not worthy of love or happiness. (looking up, with tears in my eyes) And sometimes it feels like it's winning, like it's going to consume me. (my voice cracking) But I don't want it to. I want to be happy, I want to be a good mom, I want to be a good person. (pausing, feeling a sense of desperation) I just don't know how to make it stop.

**Reasoning:** The patient's EPDS score of 28 indicates a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. Their symptoms, including <sym>persistent sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, <sym>panic</sym>, and <sym>suicidal thoughts</sym>, align with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The patient's report of suicidal thoughts is a significant safety concern that requires immediate attention and follow-up. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>

4. Provide patient with resources for <med>postpartum depression</med> support and treatment
5. Schedule follow-up appointment to monitor patient's symptoms and adjust treatment plan as needed
